question: Can a compiler-described homogeneous keyed-owner region reuse the prior owner/cache records during structural updates, reducing owner expansion work and end-to-host-commit time without changing keyed state, identity, or effect semantics?

hypotheses.primary: Compared with generic recursive owner expansion in the same ComponentStateRoot and VDOM, the keyed-owner path will reduce median update-to-host-commit time by at least 20% for rotation and one-edge replacement on at least four of five pages.
hypotheses.mechanism: For a same-key-set rotation, generated keyed-region metadata permits reusing unchanged row owner/cache records without generic per-component expansion. Edge replacement and filter changes update the keyed owner directory by added/removed keys and fall back for unsupported shapes.
hypotheses.guardrail: Filter shrink and restore must not regress by more than 10% in the median page-level paired ratio; otherwise the optimization must be restricted to the structural shapes that benefit.
hypotheses.context: React 19.3 plus React Compiler is reported as a contextual reference, not as the causal control for the runtime-only treatment.

design.armOrder: Seeded shuffle of all six arm permutations, balanced four times each across 24 measured pairs per operation; treatment and control receive identical input keys and update direction.
design.replicationUnit: Fresh visible browser page; within-page updates are repeated measures, not independent replications.
design.browserProfile: Chrome on one MacIntel device and one visible browser profile. Record browser version, OS, CPU, visibility, and DPR per page. This collection is a within-device replication, not cross-device evidence.
design.build: Production build for latency pages. Run profiler/work counters in a separate diagnostic build so instrumentation is excluded from primary latency.
design.treatmentEligibility: Compiler metadata may mark only direct homogeneous arrays of function components with explicit unique stable keys. The runtime must verify site/type, key uniqueness, stable props, cache presence, and dirty-owner status. Any failed precondition takes the existing generic path and increments a reason-specific fallback counter.

operationDefinitions.rotate: Move the first row key to the end; preserve the key set.
operationDefinitions.replace-edge: Replace one tail key with a fresh key; all other keys remain stable.
operationDefinitions.filter-half: Alternate between the full list and a deterministic 50% subset; schedule exactly 12 shrink and 12 restore samples per page.

measurements.primary: Per-page median paired difference (generic minus keyed-owner) and paired ratio (keyed-owner divided by generic) for event-to-host-commit time, grouped by operation and explicit filter direction. Summarize the five page-level values; do not pool updates across pages.
secondary: Per-page update p95 by arm and operation/direction.

Component visits, keyed-owner cache hits, owner records created/retired, fallback counts by reason, VDOM reconciliation time, host mutations, and elapsed time for the affected structural commit in a separate diagnostic pass.
One mount and teardown observation per arm and page; report descriptively and do not combine with update medians.

Output parity, stable host identity for retained keys, removal/reinsertion identity, local row state, effect setup/cleanup balance, unrelated sibling stability, duplicate-key rejection, and empty teardown.
excluded: profiler-instrumented timing as a latency claim

acceptance.primary_performance_gate: For both rotate and replace-edge, keyed-owner median update time is at least 20% lower on at least four of five pages.
acceptance.filter_guardrail: For each filter direction, median page-level paired ratio is at most 1.10; otherwise narrow eligibility or reject the general optimization.
acceptance.mechanism_gate: On rotate, generic component visits fall by at least 75% while every key remains present exactly once; the treatment records cache reuse for all retained owners.
acceptance.claim_limit: A pass supports only the named structural workloads on the tested device/profile. It does not establish smoother frames, cross-device speed, or a general React replacement.

falsification: Correctness or lifecycle contract failure rejects the treatment regardless of speed.
Large work-count reduction without the preregistered end-to-host-commit gain rejects the performance hypothesis for this runtime path.
A filter guardrail failure narrows treatment eligibility to same-key-set structural changes; it does not justify averaging the directions together.
A high fallback rate means the compiler/runtime eligibility contract is not yet useful for the named fixture.
collectionStatus: No treatment implementation or preregistered latency page has been collected. The existing V8 phase profiles are diagnostic motivation only and are not part of this experiment.
